source.title: QED: An Open-Source Multi-Agent System for Generating Mathematical Proofs on Open Problems

accepted.question_text: Can LLM-based AI systems produce original, nontrivial, expert-verified natural-language proofs for open research-level mathematical problems, rather than only solving benchmark problems whose solutions are already known?
accepted.context_brief: AI-generated proofs for open research problems

evidence.quote: We explore a central question in AI for mathematics: can AI systems produce original, nontrivial proofs for open research problems?
These results demonstrate that, with careful system design addressing known LLM weaknesses, AI can produce original, nontrivial proofs for open mathematical research.

accepted.question_text: On the two-dimensional torus T² = [−π, π]², with functions periodic in both variables with period 2π, does there exist a nonzero smooth mean-zero initial scalar θ₀(x,y) and a shear velocity field u(y,t) in L∞ in time with W^{1,1} regularity in y, satisfying ∫_T |∂_y u(y,t)| dy ≤ C, such that the solution of the transport equation θ_t + u(y,t) ∂_x θ = 0 with θ(x,y,0)=θ₀(x,y) has homogeneous H^{-1} norm bounded by C₁ e^{−C₂ t} for some constants C₁,C₂>0? Equivalently, prove either that such exponential mixing is possible or that it is impossible under these assumptions, where the homogeneous H^{-1} norm is defined by summing |θ̂(n)|²/|n|² over nonzero Fourier modes n in Z² and θ̂(n)=∫_{T²} θ(x,y)e^{−i n·(x,y)} dx dy.

evidence.quote: Problem 1. Can you find a nonzero function θ0(x, y) ∈ C∞(T2) such that ∫ T2 θ0(x, y) dx dy = 0, and there exists a velocity field u(y, t) ∈ L∞ t W1,1 y (T), that is, ∫ T |∂yu(y, t)| dy ≤ C for some constant C, satisfying the following: For the initial value problem θt + u(y, t) ∂xθ = 0, θ(x, y, 0) = θ0(x, y), (1) the solution satisfies ∥θ(t)∥H˙ −1(T2) ≤ C1e−C2t (2) for some constants C1, C2 > 0.

Here the homogeneous H˙ −1 norm is defined by ∥θ(t)∥2 H˙ −1(T2) = ∑ n∈Z2 |n|>0 1 |n|2 |θˆ(n)|2, where the Fourier coefficient θˆ(n) is given by θˆ(n) = ∫ T2 θ(x, y) e−in·(x,y) dx dy. Or, on the contrary, prove that this is not possible. Result. QED proved that exponential mixing is impossible under these conditions in Round 1.

accepted.question_text: For the advection–diffusion equation ∂_t ρ + U(t,y) ∂_x ρ = Δρ on T², assume the initial datum ρ(0,·) is nonzero, mean-zero, and belongs to L² in x and y, and assume the shear velocity satisfies ∥U∥_{L∞_t L²_y} < ∞. Must every weak solution ρ satisfy lim inf as t→∞ of ∥ρ(t)∥_{Ḣ^{-1}(T²)} divided by ∥ρ(t)∥_{L²(T²)} greater than 0?
accepted.context_brief: Batchelor scale equivalence for shear-flow advection–diffusion

evidence.quote: Problem 2. Consider the advection–diffusion equation on T2: ∂tρ + U(t, y) ∂xρ = ∆ρ. (3) Assume that 0 ̸= ρ(0, ·) ∈ L2 x,y(T2) is mean-zero, and that ∥U∥L∞t L2 y < ∞. Then for the weak solution ρ, we have lim inf t→∞ ∥ρ(t)∥H˙ −1(T2) ∥ρ(t)∥L2(T2) > 0. (4)
Result. QED proved the result in Round 3. Rounds 1 and 2 were rejected by the verifier (structural verification caught errors in both rounds).

accepted.question_text: For each integer n ≥ 0, let I_n and K_n be the modified Bessel functions arising from the modified Bessel equation r² f'' + r f' − (r²+n²)f = 0, with I_n nonsingular at zero and K_n singular at zero. For λ>0, integer l≥2, and R>0, define C_{j,λ}(R)=K'_j(R) I_j(√λ R) − √λ I'_j(√λ R) K_j(R), define C_λ(R)=√λ K_0(R) I_1(√λ R)+K_1(R) I_0(√λ R), and define F_{λ,l}(R)=l√λ R C_λ(R)[(C_{1,λ}(R)/C_{l,λ}(R)) K_l(R) I_l(√λ R) − K_1(R) I_1(√λ R)] − (1/C_λ(R))[(C_{1,λ}(R)/C_{l,λ}(R)) K_l(R) I'_l(√λ R) − K_1(R) I'_1(√λ R)]. Prove the following three claims: C_λ(R) and C_{l,λ}(R) are nonzero so F_{λ,l}(R) is well-defined for all λ>0, l≥2, and R>0; if 0<λ≤1 and l≥2 then F_{λ,l}(R) is negative and monotonically increasing for R>0; and if λ>1 and l≥2 then there exists R₁>0 such that F_{λ,l}(R) is increasing on (0,R₁), decreasing for R>R₁, and F_{λ,l}(R₁)>0.
accepted.context_brief: Qualitative analysis of a modified-Bessel-function expression

evidence.quote: For n ≥ 0, n ∈ Z, consider the following ODE: r2 d2f dr2 + r df dr − (r2 + n2)f = 0. These ODEs are so-called modified Bessel equations. As a linear second order ODE, the solution can be written as f = c1In + c2Kn, where c1 and c2 are constants. As r → 0, In has no singularity at zero, while Kn has a singularity at zero. The functions In and Kn are called modified Bessel functions.

For λ > 0, l ≥ 2, l ∈ Z, define the function Fλ,l(R) as follows (which is a rescaled version of F4 in (Feng et al., 2023)): Fλ,l(R) = l√λR Cλ(R) ( C1,λ(R) Cl,λ(R) Kl(R)Il(√λR) − K1(R)I1(√λR) ) − 1 Cλ(R) ( C1,λ(R) Cl,λ(R) Kl(R)I′l(√λR) − K1(R)I′1(√λR) ), where Cj,λ(R) = K′j(R)Ij(√λR) − √λI′j(√λR)Kj(R), and Cλ(R) = √λK0(R)I1(√λR) + K1(R)I0(√λR), and I′j(x) = d dxIj(x), K′j(x) = d dxKj(x).

1. Verify that Fλ,l(R) is well-defined for λ > 0, l ≥ 2, and R > 0. That is, Cλ(R) and Cl,λ(R) are nonzero for R > 0. 2. If 0 < λ ≤ 1 and l ≥ 2, l ∈ Z, then Fλ,l(R) is negative and monotonically increasing for R > 0. 3. If λ > 1 and l ≥ 2, l ∈ Z, then there exists R1 > 0 such that Fλ,l(R) is increasing for R ∈ (0, R1), decreasing for R > R1, and Fλ,l(R1) > 0.

Result. QED did not produce a proof for this problem. Across all 9 rounds, QED’s own verification pipeline identified errors in every attempted proof and rejected them—the system self-verified to reject its own outputs without any human intervention.

accepted.question_text: For the Allen–Cahn–Navier–Stokes-type system on T×R with x-period 2π, unknowns c,u,v,p, shear parameter A, and equations ∂_t c + A(y+u)∂_x c + v∂_y c = −(c³−c−Δc), ∂_t u + Ay∂_x u + u∂_x u + v∂_y u + Av = −∂_x p + (c³−c−Δc)∂_x c + Δu, ∂_t v + Ay∂_x v + u∂_x v + v∂_y v = −∂_y p + (c³−c−Δc)∂_y c + Δv, and ∂_x u + ∂_y v = 0, let ⟨f⟩=(1/(2π))∫_T f dx and f_{≠}=f−⟨f⟩. Given smooth H^{100} initial data (c₀,u₀,v₀) on T×R and any ε>0, prove that there exists A₀ such that whenever A>A₀, the solution satisfies ∥c_{≠}(1)∥²_{L²_{x,y}} ≤ ε, where this norm is ∫_{T×R} |c_{≠}(x,y,1)|² dx dy.

evidence.quote: We consider the following system ... ∂c ∂t + A(y + u) ∂c ∂x + v ∂c ∂y = −(c3 − c − ∆c), ∂u ∂t + Ay ∂u ∂x + u ∂u ∂x + v ∂u ∂y + Av = − ∂p ∂x + (c3 − c − ∆c) ∂c ∂x + ∆u, ∂v ∂t + Ay ∂v ∂x + u ∂v ∂x + v ∂v ∂y = − ∂p ∂y + (c3 − c − ∆c) ∂c ∂y + ∆v, ∂u ∂x + ∂v ∂y = 0. (5) Here we consider (x, y) ∈ T × R, so all functions are periodic in x with period 2π.
Suppose the initial data are (c, u, v, p)|t=0 = (c0, u0, v0, p0). We will also use the notation ⟨f⟩ = 1 2π ∫ T f dx, f̸= = f − ⟨f⟩.

prove the following: For given (c0, u0, v0) ∈ (C∞(T × R))3 ∩ (H100(T × R))3, and for any ϵ > 0, there exists A0 such that whenever A > A0, the solution to (5) satisfies ∥c̸=(1)∥2 L2 x,y ≤ ϵ. Here ∥c̸=(1)∥2 L2 x,y = ∫ T×R |c̸=(x, y, 1)|2 dx dy.

Result. QED did not produce a proof for this problem. Across all 9 rounds, QED’s own verification pipeline identified errors in every attempted proof and rejected them—the system self-verified to reject its own outputs without any human intervention.

needs_review.question_text_raw: Construct a smooth space-time weight function ψ(x,t), with auxiliary parameters, for the wave operator on a half-infinite domain satisfying strict pseudoconvexity-type inequalities, positivity conditions, and sufficient growth at infinity to establish a valid Carleman estimate.

evidence.quote: Problem statement. Construct a smooth space–time weight function ψ(x, t) (with auxiliary parameters) for the wave operator on a half-infinite domain such that it satisfies strict pseudoconvexity-type inequalities, positivity conditions, and sufficient growth at infinity to establish a valid Carleman estimate. Note: the full problem statement and proof are withheld until the corresponding mathematics paper is posted on arXiv.
